papers.summary: Abstract Synthetic riboswitches are efficient tools to render gene expression inducible by small molecules. papers.summary: Abstract The mechanisms underlying mRNA capping in non-segmented negative-strand RNA viruses, except rhabdoviruses, remain elusive. papers.summary: Abstract Mammalian telomeric DNA comprises long tracts of tandem TTAGGG repeats. papers.summary: Abstract Regulation of gene transcription based on clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) is a powerful tool for constructing synthetic gene circuits in Saccharomyces cerevisiae . papers.summary: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) organizes biochemical reactions in cells, yet whether this principle contributes to bacteriophage development has remained unclear. papers.summary: Abstract Photosynthetic efficiency, a pivotal determinant of crop yield, is governed by chloroplast development—a process that remains poorly understood in polyploid crops. papers.summary: Abstract Copy number variations (CNVs) are genomic structural variants that are strongly linked to cancer progression and genetic disorders. CNVs can be highly heterogeneous at population and tissue scale; thus, single-cell resolution detection holds great promise for studying clonal evolution and CNV-driven changes. Despite advanced sc-RNA-seq CNV detection methods, accurate methods for epigenomic single-cell modalities lag behind. papers.summary: Abstract Platinum anticancer drugs tend to target DNA whereas certain ruthenium and osmium organometallic compounds, including those with known anticancer activity, preferentially bind histone proteins in chromatin. papers.summary: Abstract CRISPR–Cas13a is mainly known as an RNA-guided RNA endonuclease. papers.summary: Abstract Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides with limited protein-coding potential, are key regulators of gene expression, yet their evolutionary conservation remains poorly understood due to rapid sequence divergence. papers.summary: Abstract The ribosomal RNA sequence governs translation dynamics, yet understanding how changes beyond the conserved catalytic centers influence kinetics and protein yield remains limited. papers.summary: Abstract Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are at the heart of most cellular processes but despite recent progress, their genome-wide analysis remains challenging. papers.summary: Abstract Recent advances in large language models have extended to genomic applications, yet model robustness relative to context is unclear. papers.summary: Abstract Secondary DNA structures in extracellular DNA are important for the function and resilience of bacterial biofilms. papers.summary: Abstract Conserved non-coding elements (CNEs) are fundamental components of gene regulatory networks in eukaryotes, yet their reliable identification across large-scale genomes and systematic evaluation of their genetic variation remains technically challenging, limiting comprehensive insights into their functional roles. papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 08 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00472-0 Analyses of tumour microenvironments (TMEs) in the context of chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T cell) therapy development typically focus on how the TME impacts CAR-T cells and how to engineer CAR-T cells to overcome barriers present in the TME. However, CAR-T cells can also alter the TME, and greater understanding of this interaction can be leveraged for the development of next-generation CAR-T cell therapies.

papers.title: Computational approaches in bioprinting processes
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 03 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00455-1 Computational simulations are emerging as powerful complements to bioprinting, enabling prediction of bioink behaviours, shear effects and printability across extrusion-based, droplet-based and light-based techniques. This Review outlines key modelling frameworks, rheological considerations, major applications and remaining challenges, highlighting how simulations can streamline workflows and guide future bioprinting advances.
